newsitem.title: USA: Fran claims at least 33 lives in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Fran claims at least 33 lives in U.S..

text.p: Hurricane Fran's wet and windy rampage across the U.S. mid-Atlantic states claimed at least 33 lives, mostly from churning floodwaters that swept away bridges and cars, officials said on Monday.
Hardest hit was North Carolina, where state emergency officials confirmed 15 deaths. Fran lashed the coast of North Carolina last week with winds clocked at more than 120 mph (185 kph).
"There were a large number of people in cars who had accidents because of the flooding," said Lisa Schell, a spokeswoman for the state's emergency operations centre.
The deaths included a Marine who drowned after becoming disoriented in the storm while trying to return to Camp LeJeune along a coastal highway.

In Virginia, a total of 11 people lost their lives when the remnants of Fran dumped more than a foot (30 cm) of rain as it moved north. Seven of the victims were in cars swept off roads by fast-rising floodwaters. Four men died while working on a storm sewer.

The Shenandoah River burst from its banks, forcing nearby residents to get around in canoes. In Washington, D.C., the Potomac River flooded the Jefferson Monument and other tourist landmarks but there were no reports of deaths or injuries.

In Pennsylvania, a couple in suburban Philadelphia drowned when flood waters trapped them in their basement on Sunday, authorities said. Local officials said more than 10 inches (25 cm) of rain fell on the area in little more than an hour.
Flooding also claimed the life of a western Pennsylvania man over the weekend, officials said.
South Carolina officials said two people died in storm-related traffic accidents. In West Virginia, where Fran dumped even more rain into already-swollen rivers, two men drowned, officials said.
